title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from this page and its neighbours. k is a principal ideal domain (Z is the model case) and K is its field of fractions. The objects are semi-simplicial ('½ simpliciaux') k-modules L., free of finite type in each degree and '∂-parfait'/'∂-projectif'. For such objects Grothendieck has obtained, on the previous pages, a Krull–Schmidt type decomposition into three families of indecomposables:
(i) Λ^iΦ_* (i ≥ 0). Here Φ_n = k^{n+1} with face maps given by restriction, so Λ^iΦ_n has rank C(n+1,i). In effect n ↦ C^{i-1}(Δ^n;k), a coinduced or 'cofree' object.
(ii) Λ^jΨ_* (j ≥ 0). Here Ψ is the rank-n piece of Φ (kernel or cokernel of the augmentation), so Λ^jΨ_n has rank C(n,j).
(iii) L(i,n) (n ≠ 0, non-unit). This is the object attached to the elementary chain complex k --n--> k placed in degrees i, i-1. It is an extension 0 → Λ^{i-1}Ψ → L(i,n) → Λ^iΨ → 0 with H_{i-1} = k/n, and it has the same Hilbert function C(n+1,i) as Λ^iΦ = L(i,1).
The multiplicities are μ_i (Λ^iΦ), ρ_i (torsion pieces L(i,n)) and ν_j (Λ^jΨ). Together with the ranks of the homology and the elementary divisors of its torsion, they determine L. up to isomorphism. This is exactly parallel to the classification of complexes of free f.g. modules over a PID by elementary complexes 0→k→0 and k→k (multiplication by n).

This page draws three consequences.
(2a) L. is flasque (= 'projectif'; 'plat' is crossed out) iff only the factors Λ^iΦ occur. These are the acyclic, coinduced pieces, corresponding to the contractible complexes k --1--> k.
(2b) L.⊗_k K is flasque iff only Λ^iΦ and L(i,n) occur, with no Λ^jΨ (j ≥ 0). The reason is that n becomes invertible in K, so L(i,n)⊗K ≅ Λ^iΦ⊗K. Equivalently, L. has torsion homology only.
(3) To determine the additive category of ∂-projective semi-simplicial modules, it suffices in principle to compute the Hom's between the indecomposables Λ^iΦ, L(i,n), Λ^jΨ. Since Λ^iΦ = L(i,1), this reduces to the two types L(i,n) and Λ^jΨ. The page then announces that one passes to the associated chain complexes.
The next page carries this out. It finds Hom(L(i,n), L.) ≅ d_i^{-1}(nL_{i-1}), which is exactly Hom of chain complexes from (k --n--> k) into the associated complex. It also finds Hom(Λ^jΨ, L.) ≅ Z_j. In other words, on ∂-projective objects the passage to the associated chain complex behaves like a fully faithful Dold–Kan-type functor. The extra maps Λ^iΦ → Λ^{i+1}Φ (wedge with T = Σe_j) are the ones later used for multiplicative structures.

Purpose: a complete structure theory (indecomposables plus Hom's) of the category of ∂-perfect semi-simplicial modules over a PID. This is preparation for studying multiplicative (cup/wedge) structures on them.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The claims in 2) are consistent with Λ^iΦ = L(i,1) being acyclic and L(i,n)⊗K ≅ Λ^iΦ⊗K when n ≠ 0.
The '(n ≥ 1)' attached to L(i,n) should presumably be read as 'i ≥ 1' (with n a nonzero non-unit), matching the later list '(i ≥ 1, j ≥ 0)'.
Listing Λ^iΦ separately from the L(i,n) is redundant if L(i,1) = Λ^iΦ. Grothendieck himself notes the reduction to two types.

ideas.what: Decomposition of ∂-perfect semi-simplicial modules over a PID into indecomposables Λ^iΦ, Λ^jΨ, L(i,n), mirroring elementary complexes over a PID
ideas.modern_name: Krull–Schmidt / elementary-divisor classification of complexes of free modules over a PID, transported to semi-simplicial modules
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical for chain complexes over a PID (Smith normal form; folklore). The semi-simplicial version has no standard credit.

ideas.what: Characterisation of flasque/projective objects as sums of Λ^iΦ, and of rationally flasque objects as those with only torsion pieces (no Λ^jΨ)
ideas.modern_name: Acyclic (contractible) objects; rational acyclicity ⇔ torsion homology

ideas.what: Reduction of the description of the additive category to Hom's between indecomposables, computed via the associated chain complex
ideas.modern_name: Fully faithful normalized-chain (Dold–Kan-like) functor on a class of semi-simplicial modules
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dold–Kan (1958) for simplicial modules. Semi-simplicial analogues appear sporadically.
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to discussions of semi-simplicial/abelianization questions in Pursuing Stacks, but not this specific statement

missed.claim: The indecomposables are built from exterior powers of the face-restriction module Φ_n = k^{n+1}, and Ψ is its rank-n piece. Λ^iΦ ≅ C^{i-1}(Δ^•), and Λ^*Ψ with the maps T∧ resembles the constant-coefficient part of Sullivan's simplicial polynomial forms Λ(dt_0..dt_n)/(Σdt). So the classification is set up on objects carrying a natural strictly commutative (exterior) multiplication over an arbitrary PID, aimed at 'structures multiplicatives'. This link to commutative cochain models is speculative and not stated on this page itself.
missed.quote: les objets indécomposables Λ^iΦ, L(i,n), Λ^jΨ_* (i≥1, j≥0)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This only matters if the later pages really develop integral, strictly commutative multiplicative models on semi-simplicial modules. Such models would interest work on E∞/commutative cochain problems. On this page alone it is only a setup.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean but essentially routine part of a structure theory: a classification over a PID transported to semi-simplicial modules. The unpublished semi-simplicial setting and its multiplicative aim are mildly interesting, but nothing here would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'K est le noyau des fonctions' is almost certainly 'K est le corps des fractions' (of k).
'(Λ^i 𝓛_*)^{H^i}' should read '(Λ^iΦ_*)^{μ_i}', i.e. factors Λ^iΦ with multiplicity μ_i. Likewise the exponents read as H^{i,ℓ} are multiplicities (ρ, ν), not cohomology.
In 3), the line likely reads 'Pour déterminer à équivalence près la catégorie additive des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂-projectifs (ou des ∂-parfaits)'.
The annotations under L(i,n) are uncertain; they probably qualify n (nonzero, non-unit).
